current_milestone.name: four_twin_peaks_enduro_reacquisition
current_milestone.capacity_evidence: The 2026-06-12 S-Works Enduro activity completed four climb-descent cycles; the current task is to reacquire final-run technical equality and next-day absorption, not to establish four-cycle capacity from zero.

latest_progression_evidence.verified_level: Session-level evidence pending next-morning absorption: four clean short Kiara descents on the S-Works Enduro, comprising two full 2K and two full 2K+ runs, with later playful runs technically better than the initial sighting runs, no late fade or rescue event, and zero braking, upper-body and leg fatigue reported at the finish.
latest_progression_evidence.physiological_context: The session lasted 139.6 minutes, climbed 508 m and carried Garmin load 174.2. Climb RPE rose across the four access climbs to 7/6/7/8, so this is meaningful repeatability evidence rather than a low-cost skills ride.
latest_progression_evidence.scope_guardrail: This proves four-short-descent Enduro quality density, not four complete Twin Peaks climb-stage cycles. The athlete-reported ability to deliver a fifth race-quality run is reserve evidence, not an executed repeatability proof.
latest_progression_evidence.next_gate: After a clean next-morning absorption response, test three complete Twin Peaks cycles with the final descent equal to the first, final climb RPE no greater than 6/10, and fueling appropriate to the longer race-specific demand before attempting the four-cycle proof.

current_milestone.success_definition: Four complete Twin Peaks climb-descent cycles with an explicit not_triggered stop-rule outcome, final-run vision, decision speed, braking precision, front tracking, and corner-exit quality equal to the first run, braking and upper-body fatigue no greater than 3/10, final climb RPE no greater than 6/10, and a clean next-morning response.

target_demands.race_day: Repeated hard stage efforts after prior-day trail exposure.

air_quality_proxy.spatial_scope: Hyperlocal outdoor PM2.5 proxy for TTDI and Bukit Kiara; a high reading is a conservative caution signal for nearby Klang Valley activity.
air_quality_proxy.spatial_guardrail: This single TTDI station cannot positively clear the whole Klang Valley or another venue. Check a venue-local source when TTDI is low but training is elsewhere.
air_quality_proxy.measurement_rule: Use AirGradient pm02 as raw current PM2.5 mass concentration in ug/m3. Do not label a single current observation as AQI or a 24-hour average, and do not silently substitute pm02_corrected if it later appears.
air_quality_proxy.measurement_guardrail: The public AirGradient raw sensor observation may differ from corrected dashboard or regulatory-reference data. Use it conservatively for exposure downshift, never as a precise medical measurement or low-value clearance.
air_quality_proxy.decision_use: Outdoor exposure modifier: combine the fresh raw point, a sufficiently dense recent window when available, current symptoms, planned ventilation, and duration. A point or window may downshift or close exposure but can never promote readiness, CNS consequence, intensity or outdoor training.
air_quality_proxy.indoor_separation_rule: Home indoor PM2.5 remains a separately sourced athlete/local-monitor surface; the TTDI outdoor station cannot verify indoor air.

sports_exercise_bands_ug_m3.basis: Direct PM2.5 exercise bands from the Australian Institute of Sport high-performance-athlete smoke guidance: below 25 normal; 25-50 moderate caution; 51-150 poor conditions; above 150 likely hazardous outdoors. These are coaching exposure bands, not AQI.

trend_requirements.guardrail: Sparse on-demand current samples cannot represent a rolling exposure window. Do not infer persistence, clearance or an AQI-equivalent category unless density and span requirements are satisfied.

enduro_egress_use.three_cycle_final_stage_option: On the Enduro, a three-cycle route can use the full DH Line as the third and final Twin Peak stage because it finishes at the car park and removes the separate partial-DH egress.
enduro_egress_use.comparison_guardrail: A full DH Line finale is a distinct, higher-consequence stage and is not interchangeable with a third Pure Quill repeat in a matched repeatability test; validate it separately before using it as a fatigued final stage.

twin_peak_stage_network.comparison_rule: Classify the stage before comparing time, Flow, Grit, physiological cost, or technical quality; Pure Quill, TnT, Flintstone, and DH Line are not interchangeable descents.

summary.race_pattern: Five climb-plus-descent loops plus an exit climb lap.

coaching_rules: Use 2024-11-03 as the main Bukit Kiara enduro race benchmark for rebuilding race-repeat fitness.
Clayton believes current DH pace potential is faster than this benchmark, but current fitness is below benchmark level.
The primary rebuild gap is sustained climb speed, between-stage recovery, and ability to repeat hard descents after repeated climbs.
Use the Stumpjumper with power meter for climb-focused Kiara loop training when the goal is fitness: repeat the same climb/descent loop, target climb power/HR/RPE consistency, and cruise the descent.
Do not use the 2025 finger fracture as a current training gate; retain it only as historical context for why 2025 progression was interrupted.
Progress Kiara durability from 3 quality loops to 4 and then 5 before simulating full race stress.

curated_jump_line_dh.interpretation: Short curated DH/jump-line exposure. Use run count, jump timing, pump quality, landing quietness, and arm/leg impact tolerance as the main coaching metrics; Garmin load can overrepresent waiting/access and underrepresent impact quality.
curated_jump_line_dh.signature: About 0.58 km and 1:30-1:40 for the race line, with roughly 55 m elevation loss.

PCP DH seeding file; main race-line lap was about 583 m, 1:36.7 elapsed, 55 m descending.
PCP DH race file; main race-line lap was about 585 m, 1:31.3 elapsed, 55 m descending.

coaching_rules: Treat PCP as a jump/scrub/pump/landing-quality venue first and an endurance venue second.
PCP is a useful impact-tolerance and high-speed timing tool, but it is not a substitute for Kiara climb-repeat fitness.
Prescribe PCP by number of quality runs and specific skill focus, not by chasing Garmin training load.
Stop PCP sessions when body position, landing quietness, braking timing, or line accuracy degrades.

access_model.training_role: Event/opportunity-based DH venue rather than a routine weekly training anchor.

uplift_or_shuttle_dh_run.signature: Usually 190-225 m descending, near-zero climbing, 4-20 min duration, and 1-3 recorded laps.
uplift_or_shuttle_dh_run.interpretation: Use descent count, braking quality, grip confidence, upper-body fatigue, and risk exposure as the main limits; Garmin load can understate impact cost when uplift removes climbing.

self_pedaled_enduro_trail_day.signature: Usually 50-182 min with substantial climbing and descending; examples range about 360-1060 m climbing and 428-1279 m descending.
self_pedaled_enduro_trail_day.interpretation: Treat as a real enduro durability day, not just DH skill. Climbing load, heat, repeated descents, braking fatigue, and late-run skill quality all matter.

short_enduro_stage_or_practice.signature: Short mixed climbing/descending effort with stage-like intensity.
short_enduro_stage_or_practice.interpretation: Classify by intent and lap notes because Garmin may show a small file with high HR/load.

Wet DH race with uplift; the race-day file was short, but the lead-in included multiple practice and trail efforts.

coaching_rules: Ask or infer whether the day is uplift/shuttle DH, self-pedaled enduro, or mixed trails before comparing load.
For uplift DH, prescribe by number of descents and technical quality rather than total ride duration alone.
For self-pedaled Bukit Dinding, treat the session like an enduro durability exposure with meaningful aerobic and upper-body cost.
Do not use race-day Garmin load alone to estimate DH violence; descending impact and braking fatigue are under-represented.

scope: race-bike chassis, braking, impact and cockpit validation
training_use_policy.density_rule: An Enduro training exposure replaces a protected MTB slot rather than stacking as an extra costly day. Official practice and racing on a declared event weekend are modeled as event exposures, not extra training touches, and require taper plus post-event recovery.

setup_feedback.ride_context: Mixed uplift and self-pedaled Enduro ride; laps 2, 5, and 7 were uplift/access laps.
setup_feedback.rider_feedback: Zeb setup was good with a bit of arm pump on descents.
setup_feedback.next_adjustment_to_test: Try 1 click more rebound damping and 1 click less low-speed compression damping at the next Bukit Dinding session.

rear_shock_setups.working_status: Both the Super Deluxe Ultimate Air and Super Deluxe Coil Ultimate are athlete-validated, immediately swappable race options. Prior back-to-back testing established closely matched overall chassis behavior, and the 2026-08-18 ride successfully revalidated the air setup under the current clipless riding context.

air.purpose: Lighter Enduro race option with subtly better athlete-perceived pumping support.
air.custom_tune: J-Tech JTC02 compression / JTR05 rebound. Athlete reports one low-speed compression shim in the air shock's damper stack was changed to complement the air spring's initial-stroke support and make the complete chassis response closely match the coil setup.
air.sag_status: Approximate athlete estimate; repeat measurement with full riding kit is required.
air.shockwiz_note: This is the ShockWiz calibration compression ratio, not a Bottomless Token count.
air.low_speed_compression_setting_raw: -7; athlete reports that moving toward more LSC made the bike unstable
air.click_reference: Unconfirmed; preserve the athlete's raw negative-click notation until its reference direction is explicitly documented.

coil.model: RockShox Super Deluxe Coil Ultimate RS-SDLC-ULT-A2
coil.rebound_setting_raw: -4 in mullet setup; -5 J-Tech original-equipment reference
coil.click_reference: Unconfirmed; preserve the athlete's raw negative-click notation until its reference direction is explicitly documented.

prior_back_to_back_validation.method: Athlete-confirmed direct back-to-back testing of the custom-tuned air and coil shocks on the same Enduro platform.
prior_back_to_back_validation.result: Differences were subtle enough that Clayton could swap between the two without a meaningful reacclimation period. The coil produced the preferred response and speed on DH lines; the air shock produced subtly better pumping support.
prior_back_to_back_validation.confidence: High for athlete-specific functional interchangeability and race-option status; moderate for generalizing either terrain advantage beyond the tested contexts.
prior_back_to_back_validation.evidence_scope: Athlete-confirmed riding validation. The exact comparison date, route, run-level telemetry and any damper dyno sheet are not currently preserved.

race_selection.coil_preference: Faster, rougher or longer DH-biased stages where repeated impacts, braking bumps and rear tracking are decisive.
race_selection.air_preference: Pumpy, pedally or compression-rich stages where rider-generated speed, platform support and the lower system weight are useful.
race_selection.mixed_course_rule: Choose the shock whose subtle advantage applies to the race's most decisive stages; do not choose from weight alone. Complete a course-specific shakedown after installation while retaining the recorded shock and tyre settings.

latest_validation.route_context: Mixed-intent Pure Quill plus 65-percent Flintstone re-entry after about one year away, with long friend waits. This was a current-state air-shock revalidation, not a new matched air-versus-coil comparison.
latest_validation.positive_evidence: No wallow, low-ride-height control problem, bottom-out, pack-down, rear kick, pitch, missed line, reactive brake, correction, rescue or near miss. Mid-stroke support was good and vision/decision speed was 9/10.
latest_validation.unresolved_evidence: Unloaded rear grip felt lower and seated ride height felt slightly lower than the coil. Very dry trail, rider loading, unknown token count and unverified sag remain confounders. Exact O-ring travel and pedal-strike outcome were not reported.
latest_validation.rider_constraint: A little Flintstone arm pump was associated with rough rock gardens and less-relaxed hands; treat rider relaxation as primary until matched evidence implicates the chassis.

rear_shock_setups.comparison_rule: The custom damper tuning makes the complete chassis responses closely matched and the athlete has validated immediate interchangeability, while the air and coil springs retain subtle terrain-specific differences. Do not demand a new equivalence proof after every swap; use a course-specific shakedown to confirm installation, pressure or preload, clicks, tyre pressures and current rider response.
rear_shock_setups.next_test: For the next race selection, keep the chosen shock fixed and complete a course-representative shakedown. Record full-kit sag or coil preload, O-ring travel where applicable, unloaded-rear tracking, pedal strikes, arm pump and final-stage precision. Change the choice only for a repeated course-relevant symptom, not a single dry-trail sensation.

specialized_enduro.power_meter_preference: Do not move the power meter here by default; Clayton prefers to ride the Enduro bike on feel.

clipless_adaptation.athlete_response: Clipless felt natural on the Enduro and possibly slightly more comfortable than flat pedals.
clipless_adaptation.comparison_context: The prior 2026-06-12 Enduro exposure used flat pedals; the 2026-08-08 re-entry followed a 57-day Enduro-specific gap while clipless skill had been developed on the Stumpjumper.
clipless_adaptation.coaching_interpretation: The primary adaptation is transfer of clipless automaticity and dynamically centred rider behavior from the Stumpjumper to the Enduro. Foot security is a secondary enabler of front-tyre authority and bike-body separation, not evidence that the pedals alone created the technical improvement.
clipless_adaptation.validation_constraint: Keep the pedal system fixed during the next matched Enduro repeat. Retain clipless as successful Enduro transfer only while release remains automatic, knee and hip response stay clean, centred posture and front tracking persist, and the rider does not rely on pulling against the pedals to correct the bike.

specialized_stumpjumper.default_role: Primary outdoor fitness and volume MTB training bike with current power meter.
specialized_stumpjumper.preferred_training_use: Routine MTB engine work, climbing repeatability, durability volume and appropriate technical training. Use the power meter for comparable climb work and control descent intent when the physiological target is primary.
specialized_stumpjumper.mileage_policy: Clayton is comfortable putting training mileage on the Stumpjumper.
specialized_stumpjumper.trainer_swap_option: Can replace the Marin SQ3 on the Elite Suito if needed.

setup_history.change: Fork rebound damping increased by one click and shock rebound damping reduced by one click.
setup_history.rider_rationale: The fork rebound increase addressed front-wheel ping over big hits that had pushed Clayton rearward; treat the slower rebound as a previously successful correction rather than an untested cause.

setup_history.change: Fork HSC one click firmer than the 2026-07-28 setting.
setup_history.positive_context: Clayton previously loved this setting at maximum attack on 2K+ through successive hits.
setup_history.negative_context: During a separate illness-fatigue period Clayton could not ride the firmer setting effectively and returned HSC one click softer.
setup_history.interpretation: Treat HSC as a provisional intent- and readiness-dependent setting: firmer attack support when fresh versus the softer compliance setting for genuinely chill riding. Validate rather than assuming either setting is universally superior.

setup_history.change: Tested the fork one click firmer in HSC than the 2026-07-28 setting while retaining the previously successful slower rebound direction.
setup_history.rider_outcome: Clayton reported a stronger dynamically centred posture, greater willingness to load the front, no leftward veer, no perceived rear wallow, more controlled corner exits, and remaining chassis headroom.
setup_history.objective_context: At the 1,118.38 m distance-synchronised overlap, the 2K lap was 11.768 seconds (5.5 percent) faster than 2026-07-25 and 7.551 seconds (3.6 percent) faster than 2026-07-28, with no lap-comparator quality flags. Power was also higher, so this is not a setup-only gain. Pure Quill was shortened by a missed exit and did not reproduce the prior 38 km/h maximum-speed condition.
setup_history.interpretation: Retain HSC +1 provisionally as the attack setting. The primary gain is improved rider centring and front-pressure authority; the firmer HSC is a credible secondary enabler by holding the front higher under larger impacts. Do not credit the result to setup alone and do not add another click.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Re-test HSC +1 on an exact familiar route at 85-90 percent with no other setup changes. Keep it only if the fork recovers between successive hits without ping, pack-down, harsh deflection, left pull, rearward hip retreat, rear wallow, kick, chassis pitch, loss of small-hit grip, or increased hand and braking fatigue.

setup_history.change: Promoted fork HSC +1 relative to the 2026-07-28 setting from provisional attack setting to the working Stumpjumper baseline for normal-readiness, familiar Bukit Kiara riding.
setup_history.rider_outcome: In a chill-pace within-ride HSC +1 / HSC -1 / HSC +1 sequence, Clayton reported that +1 felt harsher but retained greater exit commitment; -1 produced more mid-turn braking and reduced commitment to the exit. Returning to +1 on a partial final 2K confirmed the preferred control direction before focus declined.
setup_history.interpretation: The primary adaptation remains Clayton's dynamically centred posture, deliberate front loading and rapid recentering. HSC +1 is a secondary enabler that plausibly preserves chassis support so that rider skill can be expressed. HSC responds to damper shaft speed rather than trail speed, so a harsher feel at slower pace is acceptable only while tyre tracking, grip and hand/upper-body fatigue remain clean. Do not add another click or use HSC -1 as a workaround for declining focus.
setup_history.scope: Working baseline only for normal-readiness, familiar Kiara terrain. Wet roots, long rough descents, unfamiliar terrain and impaired or compromised CNS readiness remain unvalidated; impaired or compromised CNS status blocks technical testing rather than selecting a softer setting to continue.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Hold tyre pressures, fork air/sag, rebound, shock and other setup variables constant. Falsify HSC +1 if matched runs show front ping, skip, harsh lateral deflection, reduced root or small-hit grip, travel starvation, pack-down, rear kick, chassis pitch, rearward hip retreat, left pull, reactive braking, missed exits or greater hand, braking or upper-body fatigue.

power_meter_policy.default: Keep the Stumpjumper power meter available for outdoor power validation and selected structured MTB data.
power_meter_policy.enduro_bike: Use feel, RPE, HR, repeat quality, and trail notes rather than power as the primary guide.
power_meter_policy.indoor_bike: Use the Elite Suito as the main controlled indoor power source; compare with the Stumpjumper power meter only when calibration or transfer questions matter.
power_meter_policy.marin_sq3: Move the power meter to the Marin SQ3 only if outdoor hardtail power data becomes strategically useful, not for routine indoor trainer work.

calibration_notes.note: Elite Suito appears accurate up to about 200 W; above that it under-reads by about 10% based on power meter 300 W versus Suito 270 W.
calibration_notes.coaching_use: Use Suito power normally for endurance/tempo under about 200 W. For high-power indoor targets above 200 W, account for under-reading or validate against the bike power meter before using the result for FTP or anaerobic conclusions.

trainer.swap_option: Stumpjumper can replace the Marin SQ3 on the trainer when needed.

garmin_hrm_strap.role: Preferred HR source for MTB and hard outdoor rides.
garmin_hrm_strap.reason: Fenix wrist optical HR can under-read during trail riding, likely from grip tension, vibration, sweat, and arm pump.
garmin_hrm_strap.audit_rule: If a mountain bike activity has no external HEART_RATE sensor in Devices & Apps, treat HR and Garmin load as lower confidence.

athlete.goal: Progress from experienced MTB rider to expert rider.
athlete.highest_impact_objective: Build bike-specific continuity first, then enduro repeatability, then expert skill execution under fatigue.
athlete.name: Clayton

rider_category.experienced_definition: Carries speed through most corners found on trail, including rough, banked, and flat corners. Larger jumps and drops are hit frequently and with precision. Rides hard trails with consistent comfort, confidence, and precision.
rider_category.expert_definition: Upper echelon aggressive trail skill: scrubbing jumps, heavy flat landings at pace, aggressive technical terrain, repeatable speed into and out of challenging corners, and comfort with wheel slides.

work.domain: Building an AI workflow for NYSE and Nasdaq trading.
work.cognitive_demand: High: sustained analysis, workflow design, and trading-related decision work.
work.timing: Work often extends late into the Kuala Lumpur evening and may cross midnight.
work.unknowns_rule: Do not invent a work cutoff or assume the demanding workday is complete from low morning Garmin stress; collect actual start/end timing.

training_placement.preferred_rule: Train after the main sleep period and before the late U.S.-market work window; do not place hard training after work finishes in the early morning.
training_placement.current_observed_pattern: Recent MTB sessions are usually late morning to early afternoon, while indoor bike sessions commonly begin in the late afternoon before the market-work window.
training_placement.key_mtb_rule: Place consequence-bearing MTB after the best available sleep opportunity and a fresh mental-clarity check, not merely a green Body Battery.
training_placement.minimum_viable_busy_week: One controlled Suito bike touch plus one MTB exposure; preserve Sunday Sabbath and avoid replacing missed bike work with hard non-bike load.

segmented_sleep.principle: A planned nap or morning sleep extension may support a late-market schedule, but it supplements rather than erases short primary sleep or accumulated sleep debt.
segmented_sleep.garmin_limitation: Current Garmin data reports zero nap time and cannot be trusted to confirm that no nap occurred; actual nap timing, duration, inertia, and post-nap clarity require structured athlete input.
segmented_sleep.validation_window: Use a 2-3 week prospective log before promoting segmented sleep as a proven Clayton-specific recovery strategy.

wearable_context.usual_wear_pattern: Worn continuously day and night except for dress-watch substitution, normal showers, charging, or other explicitly reported removal; at home the strap may sometimes be loosened enough to interrupt optical HR while the watch remains worn.

optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.athlete_confirmed_rule: The stop and restart of Fenix wrist-HR readings define the observed optical-HR measurement-unavailable boundary at the device sample-transition resolution.
optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.physical_wear_state_rule: A wrist-HR gap does not by itself prove that the watch was removed because a loosened strap can produce the same signal loss.
optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.cause_rule: Do not assign dress-watch substitution, loose strap, shower, charging, or another cause to an individual gap without exact target-date athlete confirmation.

reported_recurring_exceptions.label: Sunday church dress-watch substitution
reported_recurring_exceptions.occurrence_rule: This recurring habit is context only. Do not instantiate or time a dated off-wrist interval without athlete-confirmed start and end times.

interpretation_rules: Intentional off-wrist time is coverage provenance, not physiological recovery evidence.
Missing or negative-sentinel samples never prove off-wrist status by themselves.
A direct target-date wrist-HR gap confirms optical-HR measurement unavailability at sample-transition resolution but does not prove physical watch removal or identify its cause.
Keep measurement availability, physical wear state, and cause attribution as separate fields.
Attribute each material unavailable run only where a strict target-date athlete-confirmed interval overlaps it; recurring context and unmatched remainders stay unexplained.
Positive low-stress use requires dense valid target-date samples from near midnight through a declared cutoff at or after 18:00, credible Garmin cadence, and no uncovered tail.
Fresh target-date wear coverage supersedes cached same-day model predictions that depended on low stress; mask them until rebuilt.
Never impute stress, Body Battery, sleep, HRV, steps, or readiness across an off-wrist interval.
Material internal unavailability withholds positive low-stress credit; high observed stress may still downshift the call.

highest_impact_focus: Build 5-6 bike-specific touches per week when recovery and calendar allow, while keeping only 2-3 sessions meaningfully costly and using 2-3 low-cost Z1/Z2 or primer touches.
Protect 2 MTB exposures per week: one quality/skill day and one durability/enduro-volume day.
Use current Garmin FTP plus RPE/HR response for one structured engine session when density supports it; keep the remaining indoor bike touches low aerobic.
Use elliptical as recovery/support only, not as the aerobic backbone of a bike-performance block.
base_rebuild.purpose: Rebuild aerobic durability, strength rhythm, and weekly repeatability for enduro practice-plus-race demands.

expert_specific_work.purpose: Progress speed, creativity, jumps/drops, heavy landings, and aggressive technical riding.

mtb_specificity.purpose: Add trail handling under fatigue, braking endurance, and enduro stage repeatability.

performance_build.purpose: Layer threshold, VO2, anaerobic repeatability, and strength-power.

history.note: Default rebuild context created with historical left pinky fracture context only.
Sunday is a Sabbath hard-rest day with no planned exercise.
Training focus shifted to enduro repeatability.

N-of-1 Garmin review found bike-specific continuity is Clayton's highest-yield lever. Maintenance floor is about 2 bike touches/week, rebuild target is 3 bike touches/week, and enduro progression should protect 2 MTB exposures/week before adding extra gym or non-bike aerobic work.

Clayton clarified that the active build target is 5-6 bike touches per week. Count unique bike days rather than split files; keep 2-3 meaningful-cost sessions and make 2-3 touches low-cost Z1/Z2 or primers. Protect 2 MTB exposures and allow a capped third when readiness and density support it.

Garmin's current operational cycling FTP is 211 W from the 2026-07-25 outdoor MTB activity with ANT+ bike power. Top-level maxFtp and the activity detail agree; Clayton confirmed auto-detection. Preserved 2026-07-16 FIT evidence directly shows a Garmin FTP update from 209 W to 214 W. Treat 211 W as current Garmin-estimated FTP, while retaining moderate confidence versus a clean steady-state or laboratory test.

mtb_heat_fueling_targets.rule: In Kuala Lumpur heat, fuel skill quality before obvious bonking; late sloppy braking, weak pumping, timid jumps, or poor line choice can be under-fuelling or heat load.

current_power_policy.policy: Use 211 W as the current Garmin operational FTP for FTP-relative prescription, validated by RPE and HR. Do not substitute the historical 222 W P20. Garmin auto-detection is operationally current but is not identical to a clean steady-state or laboratory FTP test.
current_power_policy.recent_reference: 2026-05-25 indoor tempo: 58 min, NP 133 W, P20 146 W, avg HR 120, max HR 142.

individual_adaptation_profile.core_finding: Clayton responds best to bike-specific continuity. Total load alone is misleading because elliptical/run/gym can keep load high while cycling power and cycling VO2 fall.
individual_adaptation_profile.detraining_pattern: Fitness dropped when bike-specific load/frequency fell from 2025-12 through 2026-04, despite high elliptical/non-bike load.
individual_adaptation_profile.elliptical_role: Useful for recovery and aerobic continuity, especially HR-capped, but it must not replace weekly bike touches during MTB-performance blocks.
individual_adaptation_profile.gym_role: Useful as a small durability support dose only if it does not reduce Friday/Saturday trail quality or create DOMS before key rides.

maintenance_floor.notes: The issue is multi-week bike droughts, not Sabbath or normal recovery.
maintenance_floor.counting_rule: Count unique bike days, not split activity files or doubles created only to manufacture frequency.

cns_readiness_policy.decision_role: Use CNS readiness as the technical-consequence ceiling after Sabbath and physical readiness.
cns_readiness_policy.why_it_exists: Clayton can show low or manageable training load while still having brain fog, low HRV, weak feel, slow processing, or reduced braking/line-choice precision after systemic stress, heat, illness, or dense technical riding.
cns_readiness_policy.green_signal: Mental clarity, normal vision width, fast line choice, deliberate braking release, no unclipping delay, strong/normal feel for the dose, and stable HRV/stress context.
cns_readiness_policy.yellow_signal: Motivated and physically capable, but with residual brain fog, weak feel, low HRV, elevated stress, or uncertainty about decision speed.
cns_readiness_policy.red_signal: Brain fog, sick/systemic stress, strained HRV, weak or very weak feel at low RPE, delayed processing, or confidence masking sloppy timing.
cns_readiness_policy.if_watch: Use one familiar skill target, low-to-moderate consequence, no speed hunting, no stacked setup changes, and stop when decision speed drops.
cns_readiness_policy.if_compromised_or_impaired: No speed, jumps, enduro simulation, high-consequence descending, setup testing, hard intervals, or heavy gym loading; use rest, recovery, or low-consequence repetition only.
subjective_notes_required: braking timing compared with first descent
whether the final descent decision speed matched the first

training_strategy.north_star_metric: Can Clayton ride the final descent of the day with the same aggression, braking precision, and corner-exit speed as the first one?

highest_return_shape: Five bike touches as the preferred build floor and six only when recovery and calendar support it.
Two protected MTB exposures: one quality/engine day and one durability or technical-quality day.
A capped third MTB exposure may be used for skill transfer, not another hidden hard day.
Two to three indoor low-aerobic or primer touches; at most one becomes structured engine work.
No more than three meaningful-cost sessions across bike and hard running.

preferred_days.friday: Indoor low-aerobic continuity or primer; shorten after a harder-than-written Thursday.
preferred_days.monday: Preferred social run with Clayton's wife; optional short easy bike touch only when the run remains conversational and recovery is clean.
preferred_days.saturday: Optional third MTB skill-transfer or Enduro-bike exposure; reduce ambition or skip for church/family obligations.
preferred_days.thursday: Protected MTB durability or technical-quality exposure.

weekly_architecture.race_format_proxy: Because Sunday is Sabbath, simulate enduro back-to-back demands with Friday practice-style exposure plus Saturday attack-style effort.

operating_model.coach_role: interpret evidence, resolve conflicts, and make the final coaching call
operating_model.nutrition_role: fuel training, recovery, body composition, and adaptation
operating_model.predictive_loop: Before training, store the expected session load/RPE, raw next-day response, coaching-adjusted strain response, execution-drift stress test, and schema v3 contract. After Garmin sync, compare action alignment, actual load, self-evaluation, technical outcome, explicit stop-rule outcome, review-field completion, and next-day response against the stored expectation. Keep physiology-only matches visible, but only complete contract-quality sessions calibrate the model; drifted or incomplete sessions update execution-risk and evidence-quality rules first.
operating_model.software_role: stage evidence, normalize data, apply repeatable safety rules

bike_specific_continuity.downshift_warning: Do not allow high elliptical/non-bike load to hide a bike-specific drought.
bike_specific_continuity.counting_rule: Count unique bike days, not split activity files. Any hard run counts toward the meaningful-cost cap.

cycling_vo2_rebuild.interpretation: The gap is partly genuine deconditioning and partly relative-mass and Garmin-observability effects. At current mass, unchanged historical absolute oxygen-use proxy would read about 49.8; the remaining gap is consistent with lower chronic bike load and reduced sustained aerobic continuity. MTB stochastic power, powerless Enduro rides and heat can reduce clean Garmin cycling-VO2 observation.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.recurring_build_rule: Use 5-6 unique bike days when recovery and calendar allow: 2-3 meaningful sessions including one structured aerobic-development stimulus, 2 protected MTB exposures and 2-3 low-cost continuity or primer touches. Do not make two key rides plus three recovery-only rides the recurring VO2 rebuild template.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.conference_week_2026_W35: If Monday is absorbed cleanly, Wednesday becomes 3x8 minutes of controlled tempo/torque at 165-170 W rather than another recovery-only session; Tuesday and Thursday remain low-cost touches and Friday remains the sole Enduro training exposure.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.post_conference_progression: Introduce one true VO2 session per week starting with 4x3 minutes at 225-235 W with 3 minutes easy, then progress to 5x3 before increasing interval duration. Keep only three weekly meaningful costs and protect Enduro or Denai course quality.
validation: Standardized power-to-HR response and decoupling under comparable Suito cooling and fueling.
VO2-rep power spread, cadence preservation and final RPE.
Comparable Twin Peaks climbing power and RPE drift.
Final-descent vision, braking precision, front tracking and arm-pump equality versus the first descent.
Garmin cycling VO2 trend over 4-6 weeks as a secondary outcome, not the sole target.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.weight_rule: Do not aggressively cut body mass before PDR26; fuel training and use post-race body-composition work only if it preserves power, recovery and technical quality.

elliptical_use.allowed: Recovery/support aerobic work, usually HR-capped around 120 bpm.
elliptical_use.not_allowed: Backbone modality during a bike-performance block unless trail access or logistics require it.

heart_rate_source_confidence.rule: When Devices & Apps does not show an external HEART_RATE sensor on MTB, treat wrist-HR-derived load, zones, and intensity as lower confidence.
heart_rate_source_confidence.wrist_hr_limitation: Fenix wrist optical HR may under-read during technical MTB because grip pressure, vibration, sweat, and arm pump reduce optical signal quality.

cns_readiness.rule: When CNS readiness is impaired or compromised, remove technical consequence and high intensity even if load is low or Body Battery has rebounded.

strength_training.default_dose: 1-2 short support sessions per week, 20-35 min.
strength_training.interference_rule: If gym compromises Friday/Saturday trail quality, reduce volume, load, or placement.

event_specific_sabbath_shift_policy.authorization_required: Direct athlete authorization naming the event, exact Sunday event date and exact replacement Sabbath date.
event_specific_sabbath_shift_policy.default: Without all required fields, Sunday remains hard rest.
event_specific_sabbath_shift_policy.scope: The exception applies only to the named official race event and does not authorize ordinary Sunday training, recce or future races.
event_specific_sabbath_shift_policy.replacement_rule: The exact replacement Sabbath is hard rest with no planned exercise.
event_specific_sabbath_shift_policy.density_rule: Official practice and race exposures are modeled as one event weekend; taper before it and recover after it rather than counting them as normal weekly training additions.
